service.name: Live music pricing guide for Colorado
service.serviceType: Live music for private and corporate events
service.description: Published rates and worked cost arithmetic for live music at corporate events, private parties and wedding cocktail hours across Denver, the Front Range and the Colorado resort corridor.

faqs.q: How much does a live band cost in Colorado?
faqs.a: From our published card: a solo player runs {{rate_range:solo}}, an hour of jazz duo is {{rate_hour:duo}}, a trio evening is {{rate_range:trio}}, and a quartet through a Denver evening is {{rate_range:quartet}}. The same quartet in the resort corridor is {{rate_range_resort:quartet}} with travel as its own line. Every figure includes sound sized to the venue and a named contact for the night.

faqs.q: Why do live music prices vary so much in Colorado?
faqs.a: Because the market runs in tiers and quotes cover different scopes. Marketplace commodity averages run roughly $1,600 to $2,100, and what sits inside a figure varies listing by listing. Boutique production starts at $8,000 and up. Our published card sits between them, with sound, insurance and a named contact for the night inside every figure.

faqs.q: What does the mountain premium cover?
faqs.a: Travel and lodging. The resort column runs above the Denver column because the corridor costs real money to reach: the Front Range adds $300, the I-70 corridor adds $600, and the far resorts add $600 plus lodging billed at cost. Winter passes and late strikes make the overnight the safe call at the far resorts.

faqs.q: Is a band or a DJ cheaper?
faqs.a: A DJ, once the night runs past two hours. Four hours of DJ is {{rate_4h:DJ}} against {{rate_4h:Duo}} for a duo and {{rate_4h:Quartet}} for a quartet, all published, while a single hour flips it: {{rate_hour:duo}} for an hour of jazz duo against {{rate_1h:DJ}} for the DJ. A corporate night can use both, a duo through dinner and the DJ carrying the floor, on one contract and one invoice.

faqs.q: Does booking early get a lower price?
faqs.a: No. The rates are published and the figure holds wherever the date lands, apart from two published premiums: holiday and peak weekends add 25% and New Year's Eve adds 50%. Booking early buys availability instead. Corporate holiday dates are decided August through October, and the strong Saturdays go first.
